Rechabites
REK-uh-bytes
proper noun (a clan of disciplined obedience)
From Rechab, ancestor of the clan; the descendants of Jonadab the son of Rechab, who kept their father's command to drink no wine and dwell in tents.

📖 Biblical Definition

The Rechabites were a clan descended from Jonadab the son of Rechab, who had charged his sons to drink no wine, to build no houses, sow no seed, and plant no vineyard, but to dwell in tents all their days. Generations later, in the days of Jeremiah, the LORD bade the prophet set wine before the Rechabites and tell them to drink; but they refused, saying, “We will drink no wine: for Jonadab the son of Rechab our father commanded us.” The LORD made their obedience a rebuke to faithless Judah: the sons of Jonadab kept the command of an earthly father for centuries, but Judah would not hearken to the LORD their God who rose early and spoke to them. For their faithfulness the LORD promised that Jonadab the son of Rechab should not want a man to stand before Him for ever. The dictionary marks the Rechabites for the lesson the LORD Himself drew: the steadfast keeping of a father's charge through generations, set against the covenant people's contempt for the commands of God. Their abstinence from wine was not itself a law binding on all—Scripture neither forbids wine nor commands the tent-dwelling life—but their fidelity to their father's word, unbroken across centuries, shamed a nation that would not keep the word of its God. The dictionary holds them up as a pattern of generational faithfulness and filial honour, and as a witness that the obedience men render to earthly fathers condemns the disobedience they render to the heavenly One.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The clan descended from Jonadab son of Rechab, who kept their father's charge to drink no wine and dwell in tents for centuries (Jeremiah 35); their fidelity made a rebuke to faithless Judah, and rewarded with a perpetual standing before the LORD.

expand to see more

RECHABITES, proper noun. The clan descended from Jonadab son of Rechab.

They kept their father's charge to drink no wine and dwell in tents (Jeremiah 35:6).

When Jeremiah set wine before them, they refused for their father's sake.

The LORD made their obedience a rebuke to faithless Judah (Jeremiah 35:14).

He promised Jonadab should not want a man to stand before Him for ever (Jeremiah 35:19).

📖 Key Scripture

Jer 35:6 — "But they said, We will drink no wine: for Jonadab the son of Rechab our father commanded us, saying, Ye shall drink no wine, neither ye, nor your sons for ever:"

Jer 35:14 — "The words of Jonadab the son of Rechab, that he commanded his sons not to drink wine, are performed; for unto this day they drink none, but obey their father's commandment: notwithstanding I have spoken unto you, rising early and speaking; but ye hearkened not unto me."

Jer 35:18 — "And Jeremiah said unto the house of the Rechabites, Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Because ye have obeyed the commandment of Jonadab your father, and kept all his precepts, and done according unto all that he hath commanded you:"

Jer 35:19 — "Therefore thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Jonadab the son of Rechab shall not want a man to stand before me for ever."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition; the danger is to misread the Rechabites as a law of total abstinence binding on all, missing the real lesson of generational fidelity that shames covenant-breakers.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is generational faithfulness and filial honour. One misreading turns the Rechabites into a proof-text for mandatory total abstinence from wine, as though their vow were a law for all. The dictionary corrects this: Scripture neither forbids wine (which it elsewhere calls a gift that gladdens the heart) nor commands the tent-dwelling life. The LORD did not praise the Rechabites for the content of their abstinence but for their unbroken fidelity to their father's charge across centuries.

The true lesson is the one the LORD Himself drew. The sons of Jonadab kept an earthly father's word for generations; Judah would not keep the word of its God though He rose early and spoke. Their obedience was made a living rebuke to covenant-breakers. The dictionary holds the Rechabites as a pattern of honour to fathers and of faith handed down intact from generation to generation—and as a sharp question to every people that obeys lesser authorities while despising the commandments of the LORD. The obedience men render to earthly fathers will, in the day of judgment, condemn the disobedience they rendered to the heavenly One.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From Rechab, ancestor of the clan, through Jonadab his son; a Kenite-related family marked by a disciplined, tent-dwelling, wine-abstaining rule of life.

expand to see more

Rekab, Hebrew, the ancestor of the clan, perhaps “rider” or “chariot.”

Yehonadav / Jonadab, son of Rechab, who gave the family its charge.

Associated with the Kenites, the kin of Moses' father-in-law.

Their rule: no wine, no houses, no vineyards—a tent-dwelling life.

Their fidelity rewarded with a perpetual standing before the LORD (Jeremiah 35:19).

Usage

"The pastor preached the Rechabites to shame a careless church by their generational fidelity."

"He noted that their abstinence was no law for all; the lesson was faithfulness to a father's charge."

"She taught that obedience to earthly fathers will condemn our disobedience to the heavenly One."
